title: The Missing Butterfly
author: Banasmita Pati
text:
The world was contemplating,
A senile caterpillar kipping through an entire season.
Daylight turned into
Jaded hours of darkness,
And Jack Frost ended for reasons of his own.

They anticipated his forewings,
Painted with echoes of snow and summer.
Even so,
Fanny Adams came of it—
Neither a butterfly,
Nor the wriggling grey caterpillar.

The month was summing up.
Folks started gossiping,
Spinning their own skins about the caterpillar.
Some said he lost his dreams
And transmuted into a moth to the flame.
Some even whispered
That he had crippled,
That he was evanescing.

Then at once, in a pale aurora,
When the sun itself was slumbering,
Unnoticed by watching eyes,
The cocoon began to quiver.
A bird-winged butterfly lunged forth.

While folks were amused,
Busy condemning souls,
With mighty wings and playful longings
He glided away from an old fate,
Toward the sky—
In pursuit of a soulful mate.
